title: The Last Ghost Anew
premise: Noor Marchetti, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map — is summoned by a burner phone carrying the voice of his dead mentor, Elias Voss. The voice leads him to a defector, Dr. Ilse Brandt, whose extraction before the Geneva summit is either the Office's last clean operation or a trap built from Noor's own erased past. As Noor peels back layers of forged identities, he discovers 'Voss' is a deepfake puppeteered by the defector's handler — and that Noor himself was the template for the voice. In the end, Noor chooses truth over loyalty: he burns the Office's existence to the summit delegates, saves Brandt, and walks away with the ragtag team he assembled as the only family he'll ever claim.
about_author: Noor Montrose spent a decade in diplomatic security before trading classified corridors for quiet writing rooms in Lisbon. Their fiction draws on the moral gray zones of deniable work and the families people build when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Noor Marchetti finishes scrubbing a diplomat's scandal in Vienna when his personal burner — known to no one alive — rings. The voice is Elias Voss, his mentor, dead for three years. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: cold dread cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: At the Office's unmarked chancery, Noor reports the call; Director Hale orders him to ignore it while quietly opening a file on him. Flashback establishes Voss taught Noor that loyalty outranks truth. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: institutional suspicion tightening like a collar.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Transit Lounge
chapters.summary: Following the voice's coordinates, Noor finds Dr. Ilse Brandt hiding in Istanbul, claiming she has proof the summit's security framework is compromised. She recognizes something in Noor's face she shouldn't. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: wary attraction to a mission that feels staged.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Cadence
chapters.summary: Voice-analysis expert Priya Chandra confirms the calls are synthetic but trained on private recordings only Voss possessed — recordings Noor believed he destroyed. Someone kept them. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: intellectual fascination shading into fear.

chapters.title: Extraction Protocol
chapters.summary: Hale greenlights Brandt's extraction but assigns watcher-team leader Sable Kovac to shadow Noor, officially as support, actually as leash. First ambush at the Grand Bazaar; Noor realizes the attackers wanted Brandt scared, not dead. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: adrenaline laced with paranoia.

chapters.title: What Brandt Knows
chapters.summary: On a freighter across the Aegean, Brandt reveals she helped build the deepfake program 'Choir' — and that its voice bank includes Noor himself. He denies it; she shows him a recording of his own voice saying things he never said. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity.

chapters.title: The Safehouse That Watches Back
chapters.summary: The team holes up in Athens. Small domestic moments — Priya's terrible cooking, Sable's dry humor — begin stitching strangers into something like family. Then Noor finds a second burner hidden in the walls, live and listening. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: warmth undercut by betrayal.

chapters.title: Sable's Ledger
chapters.summary: Confronted, Sable admits Hale ordered surveillance but confesses something larger: three prior extraction teams sent after Brandt never reported home. They weren't lost. They were absorbed. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: loyalty fracturing along institutional seams.

chapters.title: Choir Practice
chapters.summary: Priya traces the fake Voss to a server farm outside Sofia and finds archived voice models labeled with names — including NOOR-7, the most refined iteration yet. Someone has been rehearsing him for years. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: horror of being a draft someone else keeps revising.

chapters.title: The Handler's Hand
chapters.summary: A near-fatal drone strike forces the team into the mountains. In the wreckage Noor recovers a phone belonging to the attacker: messages from a handler codenamed CHOIRMASTER arranging the strike around Noor's habits — habits only Voss knew. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: grief weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Noor calls the burner back and holds a long, devastating conversation with the Voss-voice, testing it with false memories. It passes every test except one — a promise Voss made only to Noor, which the voice gets subtly wrong. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: mourning a man twice.

chapters.title: Geneva Draws Near
chapters.summary: With the summit nine days out, Hale summons Noor to a black site in Thessaloniki and offers him reinstatement if he delivers Brandt alone. Noor sees the trap forming and lies beautifully to his own director. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the fixer fixing his own escape.

chapters.title: Brandt's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brandt admits her defection was partly theater: she needed the Office's extraction machinery to reach the summit floor and expose Choir publicly. She offers Noor co-authorship of the truth. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: two liars negotiating honesty.

chapters.title: The Absorbed
chapters.summary: Priya decrypts the missing teams' files: operatives from prior extractions are alive, identities rewritten, working inside Choir as its human infrastructure — including, impossibly, a man wearing Voss's face. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as worse news.

chapters.title: Face to Face
chapters.summary: Noor infiltrates the Sofia farm and meets the real Elias Voss — broken, complicit, kept as Choir's calibration standard because grief makes the best training data. Voss begs him to walk away. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: fury and tenderness in the same breath.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Hale, exposed by Sable as Choir's original architect, offers Noor the ultimate trade: Voss's freedom and a clean life in exchange for delivering Brandt to the summit as bait. Noor asks for one night to decide. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: the seduction of a comfortable lie.

chapters.title: The Night Vote
chapters.summary: Noor lays everything before his makeshift family — Priya, Sable, even a freed Voss — and lets them vote on the plan. They choose the dangerous truth unanimously. Found family crystallizes into a crew. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: The team runs a triple-blind plan: Brandt goes in as apparent bait, Sable feeds Hale a doctored timeline, Priya prepares to hijack Choir's broadcast layer. Every piece depends on Noor performing his own scripted self. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: calm before the detonation.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Floor
chapters.summary: At the summit, Hale springs the trap — and Noor springs his: Choir is tricked into broadcasting its own archive, including NOOR-7 and Hale's authorship logs, to every delegate's screen. Chaos erupts mid-session. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: triumph curdling as gunfire starts.

chapters.title: CHOIRMASTER
chapters.summary: The climax: the true Choirmaster is revealed as the Office's founding patron, who engineered Noor's entire career as a controllable instrument. Noor, Voss, and Sable fight through the evacuation to sever the broadcast uplink — Voss takes a bullet doing it. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: paying loyalty's true cost.

chapters.title: After the Static
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, the summit suspends the security framework; the Office is formally disavowed. Voss survives, diminished. Hale vanishes with a drive — a thread left deliberately loose. Brandt testifies; Priya and Sable burn their old covers. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: exhausted, earned relief.

chapters.title: A New Address
chapters.summary: Months later, five people who shouldn't know each other share a slow dinner in Lisbon above an unregistered consultancy that fixes things honestly. A new burner arrives in the mail. Noor smiles, drops it in the sea, and goes back inside. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: peace, chosen daily.
